definitions.english: A scam is when someone tricks you into giving away money or property. They promise something good, but their real goal is to take what is yours.
definitions.sesotho: Boqhekanyetsi ke ha motho a u thetsa hore u fane ka chelete kapa thepa. Ba tshepisa ntho e ntle, empa sepheo sa bona sa nnete ele ho nka seo e leng sa hao.

definitions.english: Scams are lies designed to steal your money. They look real because scammers are good at pretending.
definitions.sesotho: Boqhekanyetsi ke mashano a etseditseng ho utswa chelete ea hao. A shebahala e le a nnete hobane baqhekanyetsi ba tseba ho iketsa eka ke ba nnete.

definitions.english: A scam is any offer that sounds too good to be true. If it feels wrong, it probably is.
definitions.sesotho: Boqhekanyetsi ke tlhahiso efe kapa efe e utloahalang e le ntle haholo hore e ka ba nnete. Haeba e utloahala e se nnete, mohlomong hase se nnete.

examples.english: Someone promises M10,000 if you send M500 first. That is a scam.
examples.sesotho: Motho o tshepisa M10,000 haeba u romela M500 pele. Seo ke boqhekanyetsi.

examples.english: A link says you won a prize from Econet. Real companies never ask you to pay to claim a prize.
examples.sesotho: Link e re u hapile mpho ho tswa ho Econet. Likhamphani tsa nnete ha li kope chelete hore u nke mpho.

examples.english: A person says pay M600 once a year and receive money monthly. That is a pyramid scheme.
examples.sesotho: Motho o re u lefe M600 hanngoe ka selemo ebe u fumana chelete khoeli le khoeli. Seo ke boqhekanyetsi ba pyramid.

examples.english: Someone asks you to leave your car or phone as proof. Real deals never require this.
examples.sesotho: Motho o kopa hore u sie koloi kapa fono ea hao e le bopaki. Ditumellano tsa nnete ha li hloke sena.

examples.english: A job is promised but you must pay first. Real jobs pay you, they do not charge you.
examples.sesotho: Mosebetsi o tshepisitsoe empa u tlameha ho lefa pele. Mesebetsi ea nnete ea u lefa, ha e u lefise.

misconceptions.english: Only foolish people fall for scams — FALSE! Scammers target everyone, especially people who need money.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ke batho ba senang boikarabello feela ba oelang boqhekanyetsing — HA SE NNETE! Baqhekanyetsi ba hlasela bohle, haholo batho ba hlokang chelete.

misconceptions.english: If it looks professional, it is real — FALSE! Scammers use real logos and fake websites.
misconceptions.sesotho: Haeba e shebahala e le ea profeshenale, ke ea nnete — HA SE NNETE! Baqhekanyetsi ba sebelisa matshwao a nnete le liwebosaete(website) tsa bohata.

misconceptions.english: If a friend sent it, it is safe — FALSE! Friends forward scams without knowing.
misconceptions.sesotho: Haeba motsoalle a e rometse, e bolokehile — HA SE NNETE! Metswalle e ka fetisa boqhekanyetsi ba sa elelloe, hlokomela sena.

how_to.english: Never send money before you receive a service or product.
how_to.sesotho: Seke oa romela chelete pele u fumana tshebeletso kapa sehlahisoa.

how_to.english: Never click links from people you do not know.
how_to.sesotho: Seke oa penya link ho tsoa ho batho bao u sa ba tsebeng.

how_to.english: Verify with the real company using their official phone number — not the number in the message.
how_to.sesotho: Netefatsa le khamphani ea nnete ka nomoro ea bona ea molao — eseng nomoro e leng molaetseng.

how_to.english: If something sounds too good to be true, it is.
how_to.sesotho: Haeba ntho e utloahala e le ntle haholo hore e ka ba nnete, ha se nnete.

how_to.english: Ask a trusted person before you act. A second opinion saves money.
how_to.sesotho: Botsa motho eo u mo tshepang pele u etsa letho. Maikutlo a bobeli a pholosa chelete.

how_to.english: Report the scam to the police and to the company being impersonated.
how_to.sesotho: Tlaleha boqhekanyetsi ho mapolesa le ho khamphani eo motho a iketsang eka ke eona.

why.english: Scams steal money you cannot afford to lose.
why.sesotho: Boqhekanyetsi bo utsoa chelete eo sa lokelang ho lahleheloa ke eona.

why.english: Scammers target desperate people — students, job seekers, and first-time investors.
why.sesotho: Baqhekanyetsi ba hlasela batho ba hlokang — baithuti, ba batlang mesebetsi le batsetedi ba pele.

why.english: Once money is sent, it is almost impossible to recover.
why.sesotho: Hang ha chelete e rometsoe, ho batla ho le thata ho e fumana hape.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to know the warning signs of a scam?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u batla ho tseba matshwao a boqhekanyetsi?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about how to report a scam?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue ka ho tlaleha boqhekanyetsi?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to learn how to check if an investment is real?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u batla ho ithuta ho netefatsa matsete?

situation.english: Someone says pay M600 once a year and receive money monthly from an organisation. Should you trust it?
situation.sesotho: Motho o re lefa M600 hanngoe ka selemo ebe u fumana chelete khoeli le khoeli ho tsoa mokhatlong. Na u lokela ho e tshepa?

advice.english: No. This is a classic pyramid scheme. Real investments do not work this way. If it collapses, you lose everything.
advice.sesotho: Che. Ona ke boqhekanyetsi ba pyramid. Matsete a nnete ha a sebetse tjena. Haeba e putlama, u lahlehelwa ke tsohle.

lesson.english: Monthly payouts from a joining fee are a pyramid scheme signal.
lesson.sesotho: Tefo ea khoeli le khoeli ho tsoa tefisong ea ho kena ke letshwao la boqhekanyetsi ba pyramid.

situation.english: You receive a message: you won M10,000 from Econet. Send 40% to claim it. Real?
situation.sesotho: U fumana molaetsa: u hapile M10,000 ho tsoa ho Econet. Romela 40% ho e nka. Na ke nnete?

advice.english: No. Real companies never ask you to pay to claim a prize. Econet would credit your account directly.
advice.sesotho: Che. Likhamphani tsa nnete ha li kope chelete ho nka mpho. Econet e ka kenya chelete akhaontong ea hao ka kotloloho.

lesson.english: Any prize that requires payment is a scam.
lesson.sesotho: Mpho efe kapa efe e hlokang tefo ke boqhekanyetsi.

situation.english: Someone offers you a job but says you must pay M200 for papers or training first.
situation.sesotho: Motho o u fa mosebetsi empa o re u tlameha ho lefa M200 bakeng sa lipampiri kapa thupelo pele.

advice.english: This is almost always a scam. Real employers pay you. They do not charge you to start work.
advice.sesotho: Hona hangata ke boqhekanyetsi. Bahiri ba nnete ba u lefa. Ha ba u lefise hore u qale mosebetsi.

lesson.english: You should never pay to get a job.
lesson.sesotho: Ha ua lokela ho lefa ho fumana mosebetsi.

situation.english: Someone asks you to leave your car or phone as proof you will return.
situation.sesotho: Motho o kopa hore u sie koloi kapa fono ea hao e le bopaki ba hore u tla khutla.

advice.english: Never leave your property with someone you do not fully trust. Real deals do not require this.
advice.sesotho: Seke oa sie thepa ea hao ho motho eo u sa mo tshepeng ka botlalo. Ditumellano tsa nnete ha li hloke sena.

lesson.english: If they need your property as 'proof', they are planning to take it.
lesson.sesotho: Haeba ba hloka thepa ea hao e le 'bopaki', ba rera ho e nka.
